newsitem.title: UK: High-yielding UK shares hit by dividend tax report.
newsitem.headline: High-yielding UK shares hit by dividend tax report.

text.p: British shares were hit on Monday by reports that the government was planning to abolish a tax credit on dividends, with high-yielding stocks taking the brunt of the damage, dealers said.

Utilities, which have traditionally been attractive for their high yields, were in the firing line with Severn Trent Plc down 37p to 732-1/2 by 0827 GMT. The stock went ex-dividend on Monday, magnifying its losses.
United Utilities Plc dropped 5-1/2p to 641-1/2, and Southern Electric Plc tumbled 18-1/2p to 418-1/2. Scottish Power Plc fell six to 391 and National Grid Group Plc lost three pence to 222.

The Financial Times newspaper said the government was considering abolishing a 20-percent tax credit on dividend payments for tax-exempt institutions like pension funds, charities and some insurance funds.
"The companies most impacted would be those paying high dividends as a percentage of earnings, those with poor cash flow and low dividend cover," one dealer said.
"Utilities stocks are in the front line and Severn Trent is a particularly weak market today for that reason."
British Chancellor (finance minister) Gordon Brown is due to present a special budget on July 2, which will include a windfall tax on the profits of privatised utilities.
The newspaper quoted an unnamed senior government member as saying dividend tax credit would also be abolished in the budget.
Other shares in the firing line after the news included insurers, also traditionally high-yielding stocks.
General Accident Plc fell 13-1/2p to 941, Guardian Royal Exchange Plc dropped six pence to 282-1/2. Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc fell 13-1/2p to 480.
